# data-d-money-model

- status: completed
- tldr: Lane (d): money is INTEGER cents; hybrid mutable balance guarded by trigger; canonical fns pinned empty; gaps = un-revoked deduct_call_credits + broken checkout metadata keys. Confidence medium.

LANE (d) CREDIT/BILLING MONEY MODEL - done, research-only, no writes. Answers to the 5 questions plus the client cross-check.\n\n1) MONEY AS INTEGER CENTS? YES. balance_cents/amount_cents/reserved_balance_cents all INTEGER (v1:32,107,110-111; contract:239-241). No float/numeric dollars. Per-minute PRICE tables are numeric(12,4) cent units, truncated via ::integer in reserve_credits (contract:467-468); minutes/averages numeric(10,2).\n\n2) REAL LEDGER OR DRIFTABLE COLUMN? HYBRID. credit_transactions is the ledger but not enforced append-only (service_role has DELETE; authenticated has SELECT only, billing_ownership:140-160). Balance is a MUTABLE authoritative column, NOT derived; drift is blocked by trigger protect_organization_credit_balance() gated on GUC app.credit_ledger_writer (billing_ownership:171-213), set by the canonical RPCs.\n\n3) DOUBLE-SPEND? Prevented on the canonical path by FOR UPDATE on organization_credits (contract:419-422,624-627) + partial UNIQUE index on idempotency_key (178-180) and stripe_payment_id (181-183) + release guard (640-646). GAP: credit-management add_credits falls back to non-idempotent manual_<org>_<Date.now()> (credit-management:423-425).\n\n4) NEGATIVE-BALANCE CHECK? YES. organization_credits_balance_contract (contract:249-258), replaces v1 positive_balance. No later migration loosens it.\n\n5) SECURITY DEFINER + PINNED search_path? Canonical July-13 fns: SECURITY DEFINER + SET search_path='' and service_role-only EXECUTE (contract:298-299,367-368,548-549,895-896,1001-1015). CONCERN: January v1/v2 fns are SECURITY DEFINER with NO search_path and never re-pinned for non-superseded names. deduct_call_credits (v1:291) is a credit-deducting SECURITY DEFINER fn, unpinned, no membership check, never dropped/revoked in 199 migrations => default PUBLIC EXECUTE = candidate cross-tenant drain (also get_organization_for_user/lead, check_auto_recharge).\n\nCLIENT: CreditDashboard.tsx is read-only for money (invokes credit-management get_balance/get_transactions/get_usage only, :118-128). Money mutations gated to service role (credit-management:300,347,409).\n\nCRITICAL (repo-evidenced): checkout credit path does not credit. stripe-webhook reads session.metadata.amount_cents/bonus_cents (webhook:368-369, byte-identical live copy) but the only credit checkout creator writes metadata[paid_amount_cents]/[credit_amount_cents] (credit-management:623-624). Repo-wide grep: NO file sets metadata[amount_cents]/[bonus_cents]. => totalCredits=0, add_credits RAISES on 0, error swallowed + 200 (webhook:391-396,594): customer pays, gets no credits, no Stripe retry. The validator resolvePaidCheckoutSession (_shared/credit-purchase-policy.ts:318-371) exists but is used ONLY in tests.\n\nVALIDATION: read all 8 named files in full + CreditDashboard.tsx, credit-management, stripe-webhook (repo + functions-live), billing-portal, credit-purchase-policy, call-exposure-policy. Note the named 20261102200000_billing_lock.sql does not exist; real file is 20261029200000_billing_lock.sql. Repo-wide greps confirmed the metadata mismatch, the un-revoked deduct_call_credits, and no later loosening of the balance CHECK.\n\nFOLLOW-UPS: (a) verify live grants on deduct_call_credits et al.; (b) confirm whether a live checkout creator sets amount_cents (if not, funding is broken in prod); (c) who else calls add_credits manually; (d) is there any ledger-vs-balance reconciliation job / stuck-reservation cleanup. Confidence: medium (high on the money-unit/ledger/CHECK/pinned-search_path facts; medium on live grants and the prod impact of the metadata bug).

## Artifact

**Findings**

MONEY UNIT: money IS stored as INTEGER cents in the ledger and balance. FACT: organization_credits.balance_cents INTEGER (20260124_white_label_credits.sql:32), credit_transactions.amount_cents/balance_before_cents/balance_after_cents INTEGER (:107,110,111), reserved_balance_cents/negative_balance_limit_cents INTEGER (20260713060000_credit_ledger_schema_contract.sql:239,241). No float/numeric DOLLARS anywhere on the money path. Exceptions that are numeric, not integer: per-minute PRICE tables are numeric(12,4) in cent units (20260713070000_agent_pricing_schema_contract.sql:12,26-30) and are truncated to integer via customer_price_per_min_cents::integer in reserve_credits (20260713060000...:467-468); usage averages total_minutes numeric(10,2)/avg_cost_per_call_cents numeric(10,2) (20260713065000_billing_ownership_boundary.sql:17,27).

LEDGER vs MUTABLE BALANCE: it is a HYBRID, and the balance is a MUTABLE authoritative column, NOT derived from the ledger. credit_transactions is the append-only-by-intent ledger but is not enforced append-only: authenticated gets only SELECT (billing_ownership_boundary.sql:140-144,154) while service_role is granted UPDATE/DELETE (158-160). The spendable balance lives in organization_credits.balance_cents and is written directly by each RPC; the ledger only records balance_before/after snapshots for audit. Drift is PREVENTED (not derived) by trigger protect_organization_credit_balance() (billing_ownership_boundary.sql:171-213) which rejects any INSERT/UPDATE of balance_cents/reserved_balance_cents unless session GUC app.credit_ledger_writer='credit-ledger-v1' is set; each canonical RPC sets it via set_config(...,is_local=true) (credit_ledger contract:382,573,909). So: recomputable-from-ledger = no; guarded against out-of-band writes = yes.

DOUBLE-SPEND: prevented for the canonical path. reserve_credits and finalize_call_cost both take FOR UPDATE on the per-org organization_credits row (contract:419-422,624-627) serializing one org's spending, and the ledger carries a partial UNIQUE index on idempotency_key (contract:178-180) plus on stripe_payment_id (181-183); finalize also uses a NOT EXISTS reservation_release guard (640-646). GAPS: (a) credit-management add_credits falls back to a non-idempotent key manual_<orgId>_<Date.now()> when no stripe_payment_intent_id is supplied (supabase/functions/credit-management/index.ts:423-425) so a double-submit of a manual add double-credits; the old v2 add_credits fell back to gen_random_uuid() (20260124_white_label_credits_v2_enhanced.sql:649-652) = never idempotent. (b) the idempotency unique index is GLOBAL, not scoped per organization/type (contract:178-180), an over-rejection foot-gun, not a double-spend.

NEGATIVE-BALANCE CHECK: YES. organization_credits_balance_contract CHECK (balance_cents >= CASE WHEN allow_negative_balance THEN -negative_balance_limit_cents ELSE 0 END) plus reserved_balance_cents>=0 and negative_balance_limit_cents>=0 (contract:249-258); it drops the old positive_balance CHECK (20260124_white_label_credits.sql:55). No later migration re-loosens it.

SECURITY DEFINER + search_path: the CANONICAL July-13 functions are SECURITY DEFINER with SET search_path = '' (pinned empty): check_credit_balance (contract:298-299), reserve_credits (367-368), finalize_call_cost (548-549), add_credits (895-896), plus the trim-trigger fn (135-136). Only service_role is granted EXECUTE; PUBLIC/anon/authenticated are revoked (contract:1001-1015). CAVEATS: (1) the July-1 rebuild of add_credits pins search_path to 'public','extensions','pg_temp' (not empty) (20260701133759_canonicalize_add_credits_signature.sql:24) and lacks the ledger-writer GUC; it is still dropped/replaced by the July-13 contract (contract:276), so final state is empty-pinned. (2) The January v1/v2 credit functions are SECURITY DEFINER with NO search_path at all (v1:288,401,474; v2:167,314,528,618,723) and are NEVER re-pinned or revoked for the names not superseded: deduct_call_credits (v1:291) is a credit-deducting SECURITY DEFINER function, unpinned, with no membership check, never dropped/revoked in any of the 199 migrations and therefore retains default PUBLIC EXECUTE = candidate cross-tenant credit drain; get_organization_for_user (v2:551), get_organization_for_lead (v2:571), check_auto_recharge (v2:618) are likewise unpinned/unrevoked.

CLIENT / WRITE PATHS: CreditDashboard.tsx is READ-ONLY for money - it only invokes the credit-management edge function for get_balance/get_transactions/get_usage (src/components/CreditDashboard.tsx:118-128) and never writes balance. credit-management gates money mutations to service role via assertServiceControlledCreditAction for add_credits/reserve_credits/finalize_cost (credit-management/index.ts:300,347,409; _shared/credit-purchase-policy.ts:133-142). update_settings writes only non-balance columns (credit-management/index.ts:670-686) so the ownership trigger is not tripped.

CRITICAL MONEY-LOSS (repo-evidenced): the paid-credit funding path does not credit the customer. stripe-webhook checkout.session.completed reads session.metadata.amount_cents and .bonus_cents (supabase/functions/stripe-webhook/index.ts:368-369 and byte-identical functions-live/stripe-webhook/index.ts:368-369) but the ONLY checkout.session creator for credits, credit-management create_checkout_session, writes metadata[paid_amount_cents] and metadata[credit_amount_cents] (credit-management/index.ts:623-624). A repo-wide grep finds NO file that sets metadata[amount_cents]/[bonus_cents]; billing-portal only creates mode=subscription sessions with metadata[organization_id] (billing-portal/index.ts:191-194). Net: totalCredits=0 (webhook:380), add_credits RAISES on a zero amount (contract:913-915), and the error is SWALLOWED with a 200 (webhook:391-396,594) so Stripe never retries - the customer pays and receives no credits. Related: the purpose-built validator resolvePaidCheckoutSession (re-derives from amount_total and checks payment_status/currency/credit_policy_version; _shared/credit-purchase-policy.ts:318-371) is imported only in tests and never used by the webhook (grep: only .test.ts).

SECONDARY: the one-off credit path swallows add_credits errors and returns 200 (webhook:391-396) so any transient DB failure loses paid credits with no retry (the RPC is idempotent on stripe_<event.id>, so the commented fear of double-crediting a retry is unfounded). webhook:387 passes session.payment_intent raw (object if Stripe expands it) instead of stripeId() used everywhere else.

# data-e-d2d-tables

- status: completed
- tldr: 9 d2d_ tables, 36 RLS policies confirmed; matches newest contract with 6 deviations (CASCADE vs RESTRICT, dead updated_at, missing sync/zip indexes).

Lane (e) d2d_* table conventions review complete. 9 d2d_ tables confirmed (3 core + 6 workspace; members migration is function-only). 36 RLS policies confirmed. d2d follows the NEWEST contract (20261029 phase1_org_scope) closely; deviations are ON DELETE CASCADE vs RESTRICT, no set_organization_from_user default-fill trigger, dead updated_at on messages/api_keys/webhooks, missing index on (organization_id, updated_at) for the primary property-sync query, no zip index, d2d_knocks.user_id CASCADE, and an ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING with no conflict target.

## Artifact

**Findings**

FACT: exactly 9 d2d_ tables (not ~9): d2d_territories, d2d_properties, d2d_knocks (20261102234500_door_to_door_core.sql:15,29,76) + d2d_settings, d2d_positions, d2d_messages, d2d_appointments, d2d_api_keys, d2d_webhooks (20261103020000_door_to_door_workspace.sql:19,30,44,55,67,80). 20261103023000_door_to_door_members.sql adds NO table, only d2d_company_members().
FACT: app-map claim of 36 RLS policies on d2d tables (docs/dial-smart-app-map.md:131) is CORRECT: core 3x4 (core.sql:190-193 loop) = 12, workspace 6x4 (workspace.sql:131-134 loop) = 24.
FACT: every d2d table has organization_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE and created_at/updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), except d2d_knocks (append-only: occurred_at/received_at, no updated_at) (core.sql:76-97).
FACT: every table enables RLS and creates the four org policies using the NEW single-arg helpers user_in_organization(organization_id)/is_org_admin(organization_id), identical to phase1_org_scope.sql:82-85 - the NEWEST contract, not 20260108 get_user_organizations(auth.uid()) nor 20260713* style.
FACT: every table also gets tenant_scope_guard BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE -> enforce_organization_scope() (core.sql:194-195; workspace.sql:135-136), same as phase1.
DEVIATION 1 (FACT): organizations FK uses ON DELETE CASCADE; newest core/SMS tables chose ON DELETE RESTRICT (phase1_org_scope.sql:8-11; sms_per_organization.sql). Deleting an org silently wipes canvassing history.
DEVIATION 2 (FACT): no set_organization_from_user() default-fill trigger (phase1_org_scope.sql:47-69; sms). d2d relies on the client passing organization_id every insert (host.ts:719,1796,1856,1908); an insert missing it fails RLS instead of being auto-scoped.

DEVIATION 5 (FACT, hot query): vendor/installer lookup filters (organization_id, zip) (host.ts:1394-1399) with no zip index.
NOTE (FACT): d2d_settings uses organization_id as PK (workspace.sql:20) - the one uuid-PK exception, intentional one-row-per-company.
NOTE (FACT): d2d_positions UNIQUE(organization_id,user_id) (workspace.sql:41) matched by the heartbeat upsert (host.ts:1856) - hot path covered.
NOTE (FACT): d2d_knocks.user_id NOT NULL ON DELETE CASCADE (core.sql:81) while messages/api_keys user refs use SET NULL (workspace.sql:48,49,59,70) - inconsistent retention.
THEORY (medium): d2d_knock_books_appointment uses 'ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING' with no conflict target and d2d_appointments has only a uuid PK (workspace.sql:56-57,151-154), so no conflict can occur: every status='appointment' knock inserts a NEW appointment row (possible duplicates on re-knock).

# dialpath-db-schema-org

- status: completed
- tldr: Dispatcher filters phone_numbers by user_id AND organization_id, so a fresh org gets zero numbers; no platform pool, no seed, no signup provisioning.

Node dialpath-db-schema-org DONE. Root cause confirmed: the dispatcher filters phone_numbers by BOTH user_id AND organization_id (call-dispatcher/index.ts:1170-1177, 1199-1205, 1270-1274), so a fresh org scores ZERO dialable numbers and the campaign halts with 'no_numbers_available' (index.ts:1314-1348). There is no platform-level pool to rescue it: phone_numbers.organization_id is NOT NULL (phase1_org_scope.sql:124 etc.), each number is owned by one (org,user) via FK (multi_organization_routing_contract.sql:168-172) and number is globally UNIQUE (provider_resource_ownership_boundary.sql:108-110). No org-provisioning trigger and no seed number exist: only a default-org + membership backfill (phase2_organizations.sql:184-217); grep found zero 'INSERT INTO phone_numbers' and zero auth.users triggers. Provider tables (phone_providers, provider_numbers, number_orders) are user-scoped, never org-scoped. Provider-side Retell fallback only fires if isAutomaticRetellNumberSyncCertified() is true and still syncs under the current user+org.

## Artifact

**Findings**

PHONE-NUMBER/TENANT SCHEMA (ranked):

[CRITICAL] 1. Fresh org sees ZERO dialable numbers because the dispatcher filters phone_numbers by BOTH user_id AND organization_id. supabase/functions/call-dispatcher/index.ts:1170-1177 (Retell: .eq('user_id', user.id).eq('organization_id', organizationId).eq('status','active').eq('rotation_enabled',true).not('retell_phone_id','is',null)); :1199-1205 (Telnyx: same .eq user_id + organization_id, provider='telnyx'); :1270-1274 (Retell-sync fallback: .eq('user_id', user.id).eq('organization_id', organizationId)). When availableNumbers stays empty the dispatcher logs 'no_numbers_available' and returns success:false (index.ts:1314-1348), so campaigns silently stall.

[CRITICAL/HIGH] 2. There is NO platform-level shared phone pool that could save a fresh org. phone_numbers.organization_id is NOT NULL (20260108_phase2_add_org_to_core_tables.sql:120-127; re-asserted 20260712070000_multi_organization_routing_contract.sql:146-153; final 20261029142121_phase1_org_scope.sql:124). Each row is owned by exactly one (organization_id,user_id): FK (organization_id,user_id)->organization_users (multi_organization_routing_contract.sql:168-172) and number is globally UNIQUE (20260713072000_provider_resource_ownership_boundary.sql:108-110). A number cannot be shared across orgs, so a 'pool' is necessarily per-org/per-user.

[HIGH] 3. No org-provisioning that creates numbers on signup, and no seed number. The only seeding is a 'default-org' organization + membership backfill for EXISTING users (20260108_phase2_organizations.sql:184-217; duplicated 20260109034232...sql:126-147). No INSERT INTO phone_numbers / provider_numbers anywhere in migrations (grep: 0 matches). No trigger on auth.users (grep: 0 matches). A brand-new user therefore starts with zero numbers.

[MEDIUM] 4. Org creation is client-side and provisions nothing: organizations has an INSERT policy 'Authenticated users can create organizations' WITH CHECK (auth.uid() IS NOT NULL) and organization_users self-insert as owner (20260109034232...sql:91-94, 102-108). Nothing attaches numbers or pools at creation.

[MEDIUM] 5. Retell fallback can still be empty: the sync fallback fires only when isAutomaticRetellNumberSyncCertified() && availableNumbers.length===0 && hasRetellCampaign (call-dispatcher/index.ts:1265-1269), and it syncs under the current user+org only. # dialpath-dispatcher-callerid

- status: completed
- tldr: Dead-end is index.ts:1314 (HTTP 200 no_numbers_available); sync recovery unreachable via index.ts:24 return false; empty table never reaches callerId=1929.

TRACE COMPLETE: call-dispatcher callerId resolution with an empty phone_numbers table.

DEAD-END (answer): index.ts:1314-1359. A fresh org with zero phone_numbers rows runs ONLY the global empty-pool guard -> returns HTTP 200 {success:false, status:'no_numbers_available', dispatched:0}, writes edge_function_errors (1318), raises a critical alert (1333). Not silent, not an HTTP error code.

True dead-end file:line: index.ts:24 - isAutomaticRetellNumberSyncCertified() returns literal false, making Retell auto-sync recovery (1264-1312) unreachable for every org.

Not reached on empty table: per-campaign pool + round-robin (1841-1934) and the single callerId assignment (1929, from 1928). Grep confirms 1929 is the only callerId assignment; no default/global fallback.

Tenant isolation: number queries org+user scoped (1170-1177, 1199-1205); organizationId membership-authorized (317-319; tenant-context.ts:66-84) and re-verified by assertTenantResourceOwnership (1361; tenant-context.ts:44-63). Another org's number cannot be used.

SEVERITY: (1) dead sync-recovery path medium/high; (2) HTTP 200 on total failure medium.

VALIDATION: static trace only, no live systems; all claims cite file:line. FOLLOW-UPS: upstream handling of the 200 body; intended flag for isAutomaticRetellNumberSyncCertified; consider non-200 at 1314.

## Artifact

**Findings**

1) DEAD-END: For a fresh org with ZERO phone_numbers rows, the only branch that runs is the global empty-pool guard at index.ts:1314-1359. It returns HTTP 200 with {success:false, status:'no_numbers_available', dispatched:0}, writes an edge_function_errors row (1318), and raises a critical operator alert (1333). NOT a silent skip and NOT an HTTP error status: a visible failure under status 200. 2) The Retell auto-sync recovery (1264-1312) is unreachable because isAutomaticRetellNumberSyncCertified() is hardcoded false (23-25). The true dead-end is index.ts:24. 3) Per-campaign selection 1841-1934 and the sole callerId assignment at 1928-1929 are never reached for an empty table. 4) Number queries are org+user scoped and fail-closed (1170-1177, 1199-1205); organizationId is membership-authorized (317-319, tenant-context.ts:66-84) and re-verified by assertTenantResourceOwnership (1361, tenant-context.ts:44-63), so another org's number cannot be used and NULL organization_id rows are excluded/thrown. 5) Severity: the total-dispatch failure is returned as HTTP 200, so any caller keying success off HTTP status treats it as success; only the alert + error row are reliable.

# dialpath-dispatcher-gates

- status: completed
- tldr: 12 ranked day-one dispatcher gates; top cause: cron only wakes tenants with pre-existing due queue rows, so an unseeded first launch never dials.

Day-one dispatcher gating analysis complete. Read call-dispatcher/index.ts in full (2168 lines) and traced upstream cron (automation-scheduler), tenant auth, claim/stop RPCs, and DB gates. Ranked day-one zero-dispatch causes: F1 chicken-and-egg (cron only wakes tenants with existing due queue rows; nothing seeds the queue), F2 per-lead timezone filter drops blank-state leads, F3 draft status, F4 workflow_id exclusion, F5 provider!=retell exclusion, F6 no eligible Retell number (auto-sync disabled), F7 calling-hours, F8 concurrency counts queued call_logs, F9 missing organizationId, F10 default-deny campaign_contact_releases at egress, F11 no agent. Certification flags isForceDispatch/isCallbackAutomation/isAutomaticRetellNumberSync all false.

## Artifact

**Findings**

F1 CRITICAL chicken-and-egg: automation-scheduler only wakes call-dispatcher for tenants already having due dialing_queues rows (scheduler/index.ts:63-68,74-83); it never creates queue rows, and the dispatcher is the only creator (call-dispatcher/index.ts:1076-1139). A freshly launched campaign with no queue rows dispatches 0 indefinitely unless the app invokes the dispatcher on launch. || F2 CRITICAL per-lead timezone filter drops every lead with blank state: getLeadTimezone uses state only (64-70), filter fails closed when leadTz/startHour/endHour missing (1529-1534) and reverts each claimed row to pending +15min (1537-1555). || F3 HIGH campaign must be status='active' (879,891-900); default is 'draft'. || F4 HIGH workflow_id campaigns excluded (882). || F5 HIGH provider must be null/retell (885); telnyx/assistable excluded and egress-blocked (1646-1671,1753-1782). || F6 HIGH no eligible Retell number => no_numbers_available dispatched:0 (1170-1177,1314-1358); auto Retell sync disabled (23-25,1265-1269); force_dispatch disabled (15-17,413-423). || F7 MEDIUM calling-hours: default window 09:00-17:00 + hard 19:30 ET cutoff, bypass off (350-353,564-619). || F8 MEDIUM concurrency counts queued call_logs; at_capacity dispatched:0 (1377-1425). || F9 MEDIUM requestBody.organizationId mandatory valid UUID or 500 (319,547; tenant-context.ts:16-22,66-83). || F10 MEDIUM-HIGH egress default-deny campaign_contact_releases in outbound-calling (25; gate 187-313); dispatcher catches, retries, does not count dispatched (1955-2007). || F11 MEDIUM no agent => failed (1786-1838). || F12 LOW leads must be in campaign_leads; tenant trigger rejects cross-tenant (494-496). || EXACT STOP: (a) unseeded queue => automation-scheduler/index.ts:74-83; (b) dispatcher invoked => call-dispatcher/index.ts:1532-1554, else 891-900, else 1346-1358, else egress deny (campaign-contact-release).

# dialpath-other-entrypoints

- status: completed
- tldr: All 10 number/trunk functions are 503 certification-disabled; none is a viable day-one provisioning path.

Surveyed all 10 in-scope number/trunk edge functions. RESULT: zero viable day-one provisioning paths. All 10 fail closed with a 503 certification guard: 8 return an unconditional 503 at top of serve() before try/auth (retell-phone-management:28-36, twilio-integration:34-42, setup-inbound-calls:14-22, check-number-config:13-21, remove-trunk:14-22, setup-lady-jarvis:102-110), and 3 use a hardcoded `return false` guard fn (retell-business-verification:34-36, validate-phone-numbers:67-69, enhanced-rotation-manager:19-21). telnyx-outbound-ai:133-143 is the only partial guard (503 only for make_call) but has NO buy/import/bind-number action, so it is not a provisioning path. Guards are hard-coded (no env/DB flag can flip them); enabling requires a code change. All verify_jwt settings captured from config.toml.

## Artifact

**Findings**

SURVEY RESULT: NONE of the 10 named functions is a viable day-one number-provisioning path for a fresh org. All fail closed with a 503 certification guard before any provider logic runs. 8 of 10 return an unconditional 503 at the very top of serve() (before try/auth), and 3 use a hardcoded `return false` guard function. telnyx-outbound-ai is the only non-unconditional one but it does not buy/import/bind numbers at all (it only places calls using an already-org-owned callerId), and its make_call action is itself 503-guarded. Ranked by closeness to a usable path (all still DISABLED):

1. telnyx-outbound-ai (index.ts:133-143): 503 ONLY for action==='make_call'; other actions (e.g. health_check) proceed. verify_jwt=false (config.toml:400-401). BUT it has NO purchase/import/bind-number action - it reads an existing org-owned callerId (index.ts:186-195). Severity: NOT a provisioning path; egress disabled.
2. twilio-integration (index.ts:34-42): unconditional 503 PROVIDER_ADMIN_NOT_CERTIFIED before try. verify_jwt=true (config.toml:148-149). Body would import numbers, create/list/delete SIP trunks, add/remove phone from trunk, release numbers (interface line 11) - i.e. a full provisioning surface - but ALL dead code. Severity: DISABLED (would be the strongest path if enabled).
3. retell-phone-management (index.ts:22-36): unconditional 503 PROVIDER_ADMIN_NOT_CERTIFIED, returned before try; declared actions include purchase/import/update/delete/list_available (line 12). verify_jwt=true (config.toml:120-121). Severity: DISABLED.
4. validate-phone-numbers (index.ts:67-88): guard fn isProviderPhoneInventoryTenantCertified() returns false (line 68) -> 503. verify_jwt=true (config.toml:356-359). Comment (lines 76-77) says it can import/mutate/delete numbers across sibling company accounts. Severity: DISABLED.
5. enhanced-rotation-manager (index.ts:19-33): guard fn isEnhancedRotationTenantCertified() returns false (line 20) -> 503. verify_jwt=true (config.toml:101-104). Would mutate number pools/provider. Severity: DISABLED.
6. setup-inbound-calls (index.ts:14-22): unconditional 503 CONTROL_PLANE_NOT_CERTIFIED before try. verify_jwt=true (config.toml:257-258). Would bind inbound voice webhook onto all Twilio numbers. Severity: DISABLED.
7. setup-lady-jarvis (index.ts:102-110): unconditional 503 CONTROL_PLANE_NOT_CERTIFIED before try. verify_jwt=true (config.toml:374-375). Provisions a Retell LLM + demo number. Severity: DISABLED.
8. remove-trunk (index.ts:14-22): unconditional 503 CONTROL_PLANE_NOT_CERTIFIED before try. verify_jwt=true (config.toml:266-267). Destructive trunk/number-removal. Severity: DISABLED.
9. check-number-config (index.ts:13-21): unconditional 503 PROVIDER_ADMIN_NOT_CERTIFIED before try. verify_jwt=true (config.toml:263-264). Read-only Twilio metadata. Severity: DISABLED.
10. retell-business-verification (index.ts:34-48): guard fn isRetellBusinessVerificationCertified() returns false (line 35) -> 503. verify_jwt=true (config.toml:179-182). CNAM/branded-calling prerequisite, not a number purchase. Severity: DISABLED.

KEY MECHANISM: guards are hard-coded (literal `return false` or an unconditional `return new Response(...503...)` before the try block). There is no env var, DB flag, or org-context path that can flip them; enabling any requires a code change. This is deliberate 'launch containment' (config toolbar comments repeatedly say 'Launch-quarantined in-function').
CONCLUSION: The 10 in-scope functions contain ZERO enabled alternative day-one provisioning path. Any fresh-org provisioning must come from outside this set.

# dw-callerid-derive

- status: completed
- tldr: Caller-ID and SMS sender are derived server-side from the phone_numbers pool; a Wizard campaign needs neither from_number nor sms_from_number to launch.

ANSWER (FACT, cited): Caller ID and SMS sender are DERIVED SERVER-SIDE from the phone_numbers pool; they are NOT required on the campaign, so a CampaignWizard-created campaign CAN be launch-functional without them. (1) CALLER ID: call-dispatcher computes callerId from the phone_numbers pool (live supabase/functions-live/call-dispatcher/functions/call-dispatcher/index.ts:1716; pool fetch :1019/:1051; round-robin/local-presence .deployed-call-dispatcher-v609.ts:1627-1669) and passes callerId into outbound-calling (:1732/:1768). outbound-calling REQUIRES it and never derives it (functions-live/outbound-calling/index.ts:257-266 -> 400 MISSING_CALLER_ID). The campaigns table has NO from_number column; every dispatcher campaign select omits one (:424,:734,:1317). Optional scoping only via campaign_phone_pools, and an EMPTY pool falls back to the global pool (v609:1082-1101,1588-1608), so no pool rows are required. (2) SMS SENDER: sms-messaging requires request.from (functions-live/sms-messaging/sms-messaging/index.ts:178) validated as an owned active phone_numbers row (:190-192); workflow-executor derives it via config.from_number -> campaign_phone_pools role='outbound' -> first active phone_numbers row (functions-live/workflow-executor/index.ts:860-871,911-921). (3) campaigns.sms_from_number exists but is OPTIONAL and non-blocking: only passthrough/readiness use it; a missing value is a 'warning' (critical:false, 'will use rotation') in src/hooks/useCampaignReadiness.ts:215,261-269. CampaignWizard never sets it (src/components/CampaignWizard.tsx:205-217,442-460). WHAT THE DISPATCHER REQUIRES INSTEAD: >=1 eligible phone_numbers row for the org (active; Retell needs retell_phone_id, Telnyx needs provider='telnyx'; passing rotation/spam/quarantine/daily-limit filters). Empty pool => 'no_numbers_available' (v609:1147-1176); SMS steps throw 'No from number available'.

## Artifact

**Findings**

CALLER ID IS DERIVED SERVER-SIDE BY THE DISPATCHER FROM THE phone_numbers POOL; IT IS NOT STORED ON THE CAMPAIGN. Live dispatcher supabase/functions-live/call-dispatcher/functions/call-dispatcher/index.ts:1716 const callerId = selectedNumber.number; then :1732/:1768 pass callerId into outbound-calling. Pool fetched from phone_numbers at :1019 (Retell, .not('retell_phone_id','is',null)) and :1051 (Telnyx, provider='telnyx'), filtered by rotation_enabled/is_spam/quarantine/daily-limit. Reference .deployed-call-dispatcher-v609.ts:1007-1064 fetch, :1627-1669 round-robin/local-presence selection, :1679-1692 callBody. || THE campaigns TABLE HAS NO from_number/caller-id COLUMN. All dispatcher campaign selects omit one: live :424 (id,name,calling_hours_start,calling_hours_end,timezone), :734 (id,name,agent_id,max_attempts,workflow_id,provider,telnyx_assistant_id,metadata), :1317 (id,agent_id,name,retry_delay_minutes,provider,telnyx_assistant_id,metadata,timezone,calling_hours_start,calling_hours_end). Migrations add only sms_from_number (20251213222334_...sql:3) plus sms_on_no_answer/sms_template (20251208035156_...sql:63-64); no campaigns.from_number exists. || OPTIONAL PER-CAMPAIGN SCOPING via campaign_phone_pools (campaign_id, phone_number_id, role). Dispatcher reads it live :1096; v609:1082-1101 builds campaignPoolMap and v609:1588-1608 restricts the pool to those ids. KEY: an EMPTY pool falls back to the GLOBAL pool (comment 'Empty pool = use global pool (backward compatible)'), so a campaign with no pool rows still dispatches. If a campaign HAS pool rows but none are currently eligible, dispatch is skipped (notes 'No assigned pool numbers available'). Table created 20251211041547_...sql:25. || outbound-calling REQUIRES callerId AND NEVER DERIVES IT. functions-live/outbound-calling/index.ts:117 callerId?: string; :257-266 returns HTTP 400 error_code MISSING_CALLER_ID if absent; :292 stores caller_id on the call_log; :645/:664 set Telnyx From/from; :744/:1163 set Retell from/from_number. api-gateway derives one only when a raw API caller omits it: functions-live/api-gateway/index.ts:458-482 (fallback = first active rotation_enabled phone_numbers row) and :545-559 (SMS sender fallback). || SMS SENDER AT DISPATCH IS ALSO DERIVED SERVER-SIDE, NOT FROM THE CAMPAIGN. sms-messaging requires request.from (functions-live/sms-messaging/sms-messaging/index.ts:178) and validates it is a phone_numbers row of the caller's company (:190-192), then sends from: cleanFrom (:265). workflow-executor derives the from-number in order: step config.from_number -> campaign_phone_pools where role='outbound' -> first active phone_numbers row (functions-live/workflow-executor/index.ts:860-871 for sms, :911-921 for ai_sms), throwing 'No from number available' only if all are empty (:873-875, :922-924). || campaigns.sms_from_number EXISTS BUT IS OPTIONAL/NON-BLOCKING, and CampaignWizard NEVER SETS IT. Column added 20251213222334_...sql:3. It is only passed through by api-gateway (:356 GET, :401 POST, :694) and read-but-unused by workflow-executor:146; NO server send path reads it. Readiness treats a missing value as a WARNING, not a blocker: src/hooks/useCampaignReadiness.ts:215 usingRotation = !campaign.sms_from_number and :261-269 push id 'campaign_sms_number', status 'warning', critical:false, message 'No SMS from number set (will use rotation)'. CampaignWizard state (src/components/CampaignWizard.tsx:205-217) has no from_number/sms_from_number, and its campaigns insert (:442-460) writes none. (The separate richer CampaignManager.tsx DOES collect sms_from_number: :376, :1258.) || retell_phone_id LIVES ON phone_numbers, NOT THE CAMPAIGN. Used to filter which pool numbers may place Retell calls (v609:1012; live :1059). || CONCRETE ANSWER: A CampaignWizard-created campaign CAN be launch-functional without from_number/sms_from_number. What the dispatcher requires instead is (a) at least one ELIGIBLE phone_numbers row for the org/user in the pool (active; Retell needs retell_phone_id, Telnyx needs provider='telnyx'; passing rotation_enabled/is_spam/quarantine/daily-limit filters), and optionally (b) campaign_phone_pools rows to scope numbers. The only hard value handed to outbound-calling is callerId, which the dispatcher computes. Empty pool => dispatcher returns status 'no_numbers_available' (v609:1147-1176) and SMS steps throw 'No from number available'.

## Artifact

**Findings**

TRACE OF src/components/CampaignWizard.tsx (891 lines). The wizard is a 5-step dialog (step0 profile picker; steps1-4 info/workflow/agent/launch). It is explicitly a 'Draft Mode' review-only flow: DialogTitle 'Campaign Wizard - Draft Mode' (505) and description 'Build a review-only campaign draft. It cannot launch or contact anyone.' (508).

(1) REQUIRED vs OPTIONAL: WizardState is defined at 205-217 with exactly: name, description, workflowId, agentId, callingHoursStart, callingHoursEnd, maxCallsPerDay, smsOnNoAnswer, smsTemplate, provider, telnyxAssistantId. There is NO from_number and NO sms_from_number field anywhere in the wizard (grep: 0 matches in file). canProceed() (478-486) gates: step0 = selectedProfile!==null; step1 = name.length>0; step2 = workflowId.length>0; step3 = agentId (provider retell) OR telnyxAssistantId (provider telnyx); step4 default true. handleCreate guard (430-435) re-checks the same three (name, workflowId, provider-appropriate agent id). REQUIRED to advance/submit: profile choice, name, workflowId, agent id. SILENTLY OPTIONAL (never validated, only pre-filled by applyProfile 311-323): description, callingHoursStart/End, maxCallsPerDay, smsOnNoAnswer, smsTemplate, provider itself (defaults 'retell' at 299), telnyxAssistantId when provider=retell. The wizard ALSO never collects script/copy (a campaigns.script column exists but is not in WizardState).

(2) SUBMIT PATH: handleCreate (430-476) does a single supabase.from('campaigns').insert({...}) with status:'draft' (455) and .select().single() (459-460). It then toasts 'Draft campaign created ... No calls were started.' (464-467) and calls onComplete(campaign.id); onClose() (468-469). It does NOT update status to active, does NOT call any edge function, does NOT start dispatch. FACT: insert is INSERT-only, draft-only.

(3) LEADS: The wizard NEVER calls addLeadsToCampaign or attaches leads (grep 0 matches for addLeadsToCampaign in file). A campaign can be created with zero leads. addLeadsToCampaign exists in usePredictiveDialing.ts:588-624 (inserts into campaign_leads, requires organization_id match) but it is invoked only from EnhancedLeadManager.tsx:252, never from the wizard.

(4) makeCall / edge function / dispatch: grep of the whole file for makeCall|functions.invoke|dispatch|from_number returned 0 matches. The ONLY edge-function call in the file is fetchAgents -> supabase.functions.invoke('retell-agent-management',{action:'list'}) at 350-352 (read-only list). No dispatch path exists in the wizard.

PARENT HANDLERS (onComplete): CampaignManager.tsx:2150-2153 -> loadCampaigns() + setShowWizard(false); CommandCenter.tsx:521-524 -> setShowWizard(false) + onNavigate('predictive'). Neither launches.

DB-LEVEL BLOCKER (strongest day-one failure): campaigns.organization_id is NOT NULL (migrations 20260108_phase2_add_org_to_core_tables.sql:32 ALTER ... SET NOT NULL; 20261029142121_phase1_org_scope.sql:123) and a BEFORE INSERT trigger campaigns_require_authoritative_tenant (20260712070000_multi_organization_routing_contract.sql:398-401) calls enforce_tenant_owned_core_resource() which RAISES EXCEPTION '... requires an explicit organization_id' when NEW.organization_id IS NULL (lines 379-382). handleCreate's insert object (442-460) sets user_id, name, description, workflow_id, agent_id, calling_hours_start/end, max_calls_per_day, sms_on_no_answer, sms_template, status, provider, telnyx_assistant_id - and DOES NOT set organization_id. The two sibling campaign creators DO set it: CampaignManager.handleCloneCampaign sets organization_id at 559; CampaignSetupWizard.handleCreateCampaign sets organization_id at 159 (and even guards !organizationId at 153). # dw-dispatch-reach

- status: completed
- tldr: No browser component can start a real first-campaign call: UI gate browserCallDispatchAllowed()=false AND server rejects browser campaign calls at outbound-calling:364-368.

DONE: Determine whether any browser component can start a real outbound call for a first campaign, and where it dies.
TOUCHED: none (research only).
EVIDENCE: see artifact evidence list (key: outbound-calling/index.ts:364-368; launchSafety.ts:128-133; CampaignManager.tsx:780/:727; CallCenter.tsx:101 + zero importers; useCallDispatcher.ts:109/:199).
RESULT: NO browser component can start a real outbound call for a first campaign. makeCall (usePredictiveDialing.ts:663) has no internal guard and always sends campaignId + a user JWT. Its mounted caller (CampaignManager.handleStartCall:780) is blocked by browserCallDispatchAllowed()=false; its ungated caller (CallCenter.tsx:101) is unmounted dead code. Even if reached, the server definitively rejects browser campaign calls at outbound-calling:364-368 ("Campaign calls require the service dispatcher and an exact atomic queue claim"), plus requires an active campaign (:379) that the browser cannot activate, and a default-deny contact release (:926-943). Only call-dispatcher -> outbound-calling (service role + queueId + dispatchGeneration, call-dispatcher:1939-1961) can dial, and that dispatcher is client-gated by the same false flag.
COULD_NOT: verify DB/seed state, campaign_contact_release RPC SQL, or other dial edge functions (research-only, no live reads).
CONFIDENCE: high (reachability + server block); medium on contact-release specifics.

## Artifact

**Findings**

makeCall has NO internal launch-lock guard and always sends campaignId + caller JWT. Of its two UI callers, CampaignManager.handleStartCall is gated by browserCallDispatchAllowed() (which hardcodes false); CallCenter.handleStartCall is UNgated but CallCenter.tsx is unmounted dead code with zero importers. Independently, the server hard-rejects any browser JWT campaign create_call at outbound-calling:364-368 ('Campaign calls require the service dispatcher and an exact atomic queue claim'), and also requires campaign.status==='active' (:379) which the browser cannot set (activation is launch-locked). Therefore NO browser component can start a real outbound call for a first campaign. The only dialing path is call-dispatcher -> outbound-calling with the service-role key + queueId + dispatchGeneration; that dispatcher is reachable by an auth'd user from the browser only through useCallDispatcher, which is itself blocked by browserCallDispatchAllowed(). RANKED FAILURES: (1) CRITICAL outbound-calling:364-368 server reject. (2) CRITICAL launchSafety.ts:128-133 false gate blocks all mounted dispatch (CampaignManager:780/:727, useCallDispatcher:109/:199). (3) HIGH campaign must be 'active' (:379) but a fresh campaign is 'draft' and activation is launch-locked. (4) HIGH default-deny campaign contact release (:926-943). (5) MED caller rotation_enabled===true + retell_phone_id (:476/:490) and calling-hours/tz (:765-790) and credits (:946-1043). (6) LOW/DEAD CallCenter.tsx:76-120 ungated but unreachable.

# dw-quicklaunch

- status: completed
- tldr: All 3 browser launch paths are no-ops; real egress is server-side only; top risk = addTestLead writes live leads with no lock

DONE: Traced the QuickLaunch flow. All three browser launch surfaces are intentionally non-executing. (1) QuickLaunchButton.handleLaunch (QuickLaunchButton.tsx:102-114) never dispatches: demo = toast only, else calls onLaunch if given, and it is mounted at Dashboard.tsx:278 with NO onLaunch prop, so it is a production no-op. checkReadiness (:35-101) only checks ANY campaign's agent_id (:61-66), ANY active number (:76-81), and non-DNC lead count (:69-73) - not the target campaign, provider binding, script, or hours. (2) QuickTestCampaign.activateCampaignAndDispatch (QuickTestCampaign.tsx:162-180) is a pure no-op: validates selectedCampaign only, then toasts the launch-lock message; button labeled 'Activation Locked'. No status update or edge call. (3) Required vs optional: readiness hook criticals = campaign name, Retell-imported numbers, wait/SMS/agent checks (agent+phone checks apply ONLY if the workflow has call steps), leads attached, timezone. Optional/warning = A2P, webhook, calling hours. Script is never validated anywhere in this path; from_number only 'any active number exists'. (4) No browser path reaches a phone number: launchSafety.ts hardcodes browserCallDispatchAllowed()/browserContactEgressAllowed() = false, and useCallDispatcher (:109-118,:199-206) early-returns on that gate. Real egress is server-side only: call-dispatcher dials 'active' campaigns via outbound-calling (:1955), Retell only (Telnyx :1647-1666 and Assistable :1754-1777 blocked).\n\nTOP DAY-ONE RISK (THEORY): QuickTestCampaign.addTestLead (:55-161) writes a real phone number into campaign_leads (:131-138) and can reset a lead to 'new' (:97-101) with NO launch lock; if that campaign is already server-activated, the next dispatcher tick could call it. No campaign_leads INSERT trigger found.\n\nVALIDATION: static source trace of the 4 files + launchSafety.ts + useCallDispatcher.ts + useCampaignReadiness.ts + call-dispatcher edge fn; no live-system calls.\n\nFOLLOW-UPS: (a) confirm call-dispatcher's timer/cadence; (b) confirm outbound-calling's own consent/DNC/global-stop re-checks; (c) check RLS on leads/campaign_leads; (d) inspect ReadinessFixDialogs write paths on active campaigns.

## Artifact

**Findings**

1) QuickLaunchButton.checkReadiness (QuickLaunchButton.tsx:35-101) computes 3 booleans only: hasAgent = ANY campaign row with non-null agent_id (:61-66); hasLeads = count of non-DNC leads (:69-73); hasPhoneNumber = ANY active phone_numbers row (:76-81). isReady = all three (:91). It does NOT check the specific campaign being launched, agent/provider binding, script, hours, or egress certification. Demo mode hardcodes isReady:true (:38-49). 2) QuickLaunchButton.handleLaunch (:102-114) NEVER dispatches. Demo -> toast only + return (:103-109). Non-demo -> calls props.onLaunch() if provided (:111-113); with no onLaunch prop it is a pure no-op. Mounted at Dashboard.tsx:278 as <QuickLaunchButton /> with NO onLaunch prop, so in production the button does nothing. Even the ready-state button is labeled 'Review Launch Requirements' (:154) and shows 'Launch certification is still required' (:144) + CAMPAIGN_ACTIVATION_LAUNCH_LOCK_MESSAGE (:173). 3) QuickTestCampaign.activateCampaignAndDispatch (:162-180) is a deliberate no-op: validates only selectedCampaign truthiness (:163-170), then sets lastAction + toasts the launch-lock message (:172-178). No status update, no edge-function invoke, no provider call. Button labeled 'Activation Locked' (:268). 4) QuickTestCampaign.addTestLead (:55-161) DOES write live data: validates selectedCampaign+testPhone (:56-63), requires userId+organizationId (:69-70), verifies campaign ownership (:72-79), formats phone to E.164 (:81), then either RESETS an existing lead to status:'new' (:94-101) or INSERTS a new lead (first_name 'Test') (:102-119), then inserts a campaign_leads row (:129-139). It changes NO campaign activation state and applies no launch lock. 5) Config required vs optional (useCampaignReadiness, src/hooks/useCampaignReadiness.ts): CRITICAL = campaign_name; retell_phone_numbers (0 usable active numbers with retell_phone_id); wait_steps_config (only if workflow has wait steps); sms_phone_number + ai_sms_settings (only if SMS steps); ai_agent (agent_id) + agent_phone + caller_id_retell (ALL only if workflow has CALL steps); leads_assigned; timezone_coverage (critical only when ALL campaign leads lack state AND no campaign timezone). OPTIONAL/warning = a2p_registration, campaign_sms_number, webhook, calling_hours (defaults 9-5). A campaign with NO workflow steps bypasses every agent/phone/SMS check; leads_assigned still always runs. 6) Script is NEVER validated by any of the four components nor by the readiness hook; from_number is only 'any active number exists' (QuickLaunchButton.tsx:76-81), not campaign/provider-bound; calling_hours optional. 7) No browser path reaches a phone number: launchSafety.ts hardcodes browserCallDispatchAllowed()=false, browserContactEgressAllowed()=false, browserAutonomousActionAllowed()=false, browserProviderAdministrationAllowed()=false; browserCampaignStatusMutationAllowed()=true only for 'paused'. useCallDispatcher.dispatchCalls (:109-118) and startAutoDispatch (:199-206) early-return on the false gate before invoking call-dispatcher; forceRequeue/forceDispatch/resetSchedule only toast lock messages (:260-295). 8) The only real egress is server-side call-dispatcher: considers status='active' campaigns only (:891) and invokes outbound-calling (:1955); Telnyx blocked (:1647-1666), Assistable blocked (:1754-1777); Retell = sole launch-certified provider (:883); force/callback/auto-sync gates hardcoded false (:15-25). 9) Highest day-one risk (THEORY): addTestLead inserts a real phone number into campaign_leads on ANY selected campaign (:131-138) and can flip an existing lead back to 'new' (:97-101) with no launch lock; if that campaign is already status='active', the next server dispatcher tick could place a real Retell call/SMS. No DB trigger on campaign_leads INSERT found (only updated_at), so dispatch is poll-driven.

# dw-status-activate

- status: completed
- tldr: One live path activates a campaign: api-gateway POST /v1/campaigns/:id/launch (campaigns:write + owner); UI is fully locked; canary path never writes.

dw-status-activate DONE. Question: is there any path (UI or server) that promotes a draft campaign to active today, and what does it require?

ANSWER: Yes, exactly one. `POST /v1/campaigns/:id/launch` on the external REST api-gateway (supabase/functions-live/api-gateway/index.ts:188) -> setCampaignStatus (same file:361-369), needs only an API key with `campaigns:write` and campaign user_id ownership. Exposed as MCP tool `dialsmart_launch_campaign` (mcp-server/src/tools/campaigns.ts:32-41). No consent/DNC/balance/global-stop promotion engine exists. Only extra constraint: live-only trigger trg_guard_campaign_has_agent (docs/wholesale/audit/phase1/live_only/20260828014640_campaign_launch_guard.sql:2-22) requires an assigned agent. Same function can also CREATE an active campaign via body.status (index.ts:387).

NO UI path: every browser writer is launch-locked (src/lib/launchSafety.ts:115-119 allows 'paused' only; src/hooks/usePredictiveDialing.ts:521-529; src/components/CampaignManager.tsx:499-518; CampaignLauncher.tsx:231-247; QuickTestCampaign.tsx:162-179). Repo test enforces this but scans src only (scripts/validate-campaign-bundle.test.mjs:589-602).

NO SQL/RPC/trigger writer. ai-assistant's ungated update_campaign (supabase/functions/ai-assistant/index.ts:900-917) is dead behind a 503 at :2891-2901. The canary path is read-only and never touches Supabase (campaigns/solar-exit/reference/CANARY-PROMOTION-ENGINE.md:3,26,28).

MATERIAL SIDE-FINDING: the EXTERNAL_API_NOT_CERTIFIED gate that LIVE-VS-MAIN-GATES.md:21 attributes to api-gateway@149 is absent from both api-gateway copies on disk, while 73 sibling functions keep their gates.

## Artifact

**Findings**

ANSWER: YES -- exactly one reachable path promotes a draft campaign to 'active' today, and it is a server-side REST/MCP route, not the UI.

(1) THE ONE PATH. `POST /v1/campaigns/:id/launch` on the external REST api-gateway (also exposed as the MCP tool `dialsmart_launch_campaign`). It requires only: (a) a valid API key (dsk_live_...) carrying the `campaigns:write` scope, and (b) the campaign to belong to that key's user_id. It performs a bare `update({status:'active'})`. There is NO consent / DNC / jurisdiction / provider-version / balance / global-stop promotion engine behind it. The only additional constraint is a live-only Postgres trigger that requires an agent_id or telnyx_assistant_id to be set when status becomes 'active'. The 'audited server-side promotion' the UI promises (src/lib/launchSafety.ts:15-16) does not exist in this repository.

(2) NO UI PATH. Every browser writer is launch-locked: browserCampaignStatusMutationAllowed allows only 'paused' (src/lib/launchSafety.ts:115-119); usePredictiveDialing.updateCampaign blocks non-paused status (src/hooks/usePredictiveDialing.ts:521-529); CampaignManager.handleStatusChange hard-locks 'active' (src/components/CampaignManager.tsx:499-518); CampaignLauncher.launchCampaign (src/components/CampaignLauncher.tsx:231-247) and QuickTestCampaign.activateCampaignAndDispatch (src/components/QuickTestCampaign.tsx:162-179) only show lock toasts; AutonomousAgentDashboard sets 'paused' only (src/components/AutonomousAgentDashboard.tsx:674). A repo test enforces this, but scans src only (scripts/validate-campaign-bundle.test.mjs:589-602).

(3) NO SQL/RPC/TRIGGER WRITER. Nothing in supabase/ or certification/ sets campaigns.status='active'. The only SQL referencing campaign status plus 'active' are readers/decisions: supabase/migrations/20260713064000_dialing_queue_mutation_boundary.sql:251 and supabase/migrations/20260713150000_campaign_contact_release_gate.sql:266 (the release gate is downstream of activation, not a gate on it).

(4) SECOND SERVER WRITER THAT IS DEAD. supabase/functions/ai-assistant/index.ts:900-917 update_campaign copies args.status verbatim with no allowlist, but the whole function 503s before auth at :2891-2901 (AI_ASSISTANT_TOOL_SURFACE_NOT_TENANT_CERTIFIED). It is not deployed in functions-live/ at all.

(5) THE CANARY PATH IS NOT A WRITER. campaigns/solar-exit/reference/CANARY-PROMOTION-ENGINE.md:3,26,28 -- read-only, stdout-only, never touches Supabase/Retell/GHL/a lead, authorization_scope 'evidence_chain_only', launch_authorized false. A 'promote'/'normal' verdict is evidence for an external trust root; nothing in the repo consumes it to flip campaigns.status.

(6) MATERIAL DISCREPANCY. docs/wholesale/audit/phase1/LIVE-VS-MAIN-GATES.md:21 attributes an api-gateway gate (EXTERNAL_API_NOT_CERTIFIED@149, 503s every request before routing) to main. That gate string is absent from both api-gateway copies on this working tree and from api-gateway/_shared, while 73 other *_NOT_CERTIFIED markers exist under supabase/functions/. So on this checkout the launch route is unguarded in both the main/containment profile and the live snapshot, and LIVE-VS-MAIN-GATES.md:53 independently confirms live api-gateway (v35) has no gate and answers /v1/health with HTTP 200.

SECOND INSERT-SIDE PATH (same function): api-gateway createCampaign (supabase/functions-live/api-gateway/index.ts:383-399) sets `status: body.status ?? "draft"`, i.e. POST /v1/campaigns can also CREATE an already-active campaign if the caller passes status:'active'. It too is guarded only by the same DB trigger.

## Artifact

**Findings**

ai-assistant/index.ts (3008 lines). KEY GATING FACT: serve() calls isAiAssistantToolSurfaceTenantCertified() (2891) which is hardcoded to return false (2878-2880), so in production the function ALWAYS short-circuits to a 503 before auth, and none of the 6 auth checks, tool code, or its 17 catch blocks are reachable.

(1) HTTP RESPONSE SHAPES. SUCCESS bodies carry NO status (Deno default 200) and NO `success` key: main text path -> {response, analytics} (3082-3085); tool path -> {response, actions_taken, analytics} (3075-3079); confirmation path -> {response, pending_actions, analytics} (3032-3036); OPTIONS preflight -> null body, corsHeaders only (2884). ERROR bodies are INCONSISTENT: plain errors use {error} only -> 401 Unauthorized (2906,2945,2952), 400 Message required (2917), 500 'AI not configured' (2923), 500 'Supabase configuration missing' (2931), 429 'Rate limited' (2988), 500 generic {error: error.message} (3089); the two 'containment' errors use a DIFFERENT shape {success:false, disabled:true, error_code, error} -> 503 (2892-2900) and 503 (3004-3012). {success}/{message} exist ONLY inside executeToolCall return objects (folded into response text/actions_taken), never at HTTP top level.

(2) SWALLOWED FAILURES. No `.catch(` promise handlers exist anywhere (grep: 0). Only one bare empty-ish catch: 3020-3024 `catch { args = {}; }` swallows JSON.parse failure. Catches that continue and still report SUCCESS (TRUE swallows): 1100-1102 (alt-number fetch fails -> console.error, falls through, no rethrow); 1269-1271 (per-lead blast send -> `failCount++` ONLY, no log, error discarded); 2135-2137 (agent list fetch -> console.error, continues); 2267-2274 (voice-broadcast-engine trigger -> console.error, still returns success:true 'now LIVE'); 2315-2318 (retell agent verify -> console.error, continues); 2350-2357 (call-dispatcher trigger -> console.error, still returns success:true 'now ACTIVE'); 2405-2419 (workflow_steps insert error -> console.error only, still returns success:true 'Workflow Created'). Catches that return a graceful {success:false} object (not rethrown, so HTTP stays 200): 964-968, 1023-1027, 1126-1134, 1173-1175, 1360-1363, 1862-1865 (warnings.push), 1886-1889 (warnings.push), 1960-1963, 2656-2659. Main handler catch 3087-3091 logs + returns 500 (correct). Fire-and-forget / result-ignored awaits (no response.ok check or error check): 2259-2266, 2336-2349, 2207 (campaign_leads insert), 2835-2838, 2841-2845, 1345-1354, 1112-1119, 1075-1078, 1129-1132. console.error with no rethrow at 966,1025,1101,1128,1863,1887,1957,2136,2268,2316,2351,2406,2594,2657,2740,2771,3088.

(3) CORS / SECRETS / ENV. corsHeaders (11-14) = {Access-Control-Allow-Origin:'*', Access-Control-Allow-Headers:'authorization, x-client-info, apikey, content-type'}; NO Access-Control-Allow-Methods header. OPTIONS returns null body (2884). Every response spreads ...corsHeaders + Content-Type: application/json. Env read via Deno.env.get: LOVABLE_API_KEY (2921) fail-fast 500 if missing (2923); SUPABASE_URL + SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY (2927-2928) fail-fast 500 (2931); TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID/AUTH_TOKEN read at 920-921,972-973,1138-1139,1287-1288,1790-1791,1916-1917 and null-checked per-tool returning {success:false} (975,1141,1290) or guarded by `&&` (1928); RETELL_AI_API_KEY read at 1792,1915,2107,2306 and guarded by `if (retellApiKey)` (1869,2107,2307). MISMATCH: inside buy_phone_numbers (2621-2622) and the two trigger fetches (2256-2257, 2333-2334) SUPABASE_URL/SERVICE_ROLE_KEY are re-read with NO null check, so if unset fetch() hits the literal string 'undefined/...' and throws -> swallowed by the local try (2267/2350) or the buy catch (2656). Secrets are only interpolated into Authorization headers (Bearer ${serviceKey}, Basic btoa(sid:token)); no console.log of secret values found (677 logs toolName+args, 1060 logs phone numbers only).

## Artifact

**Findings**

FILE: dial-smart-system/supabase/functions/ai-sms-processor/index.ts (Deno/Supabase Edge Function, 1215 lines).

(1) HTTP RESPONSE SHAPES
SUCCESS: every success returns HTTP 200 (some omit the status key entirely, which defaults to 200). Standard success body is {success:true, ...}. Variants:
- {success:true,message} DNC skip lines 210-219; AI-disabled lines 324-332; human-reply-pause lines 355-363; 'Processed without response' lines 384-392.
- {success:true,message:'Processed and responded',response} lines 372-381.

- {success:true,smsPrompt} lines 720-728.
- OPTIONS preflight: new Response(null,{headers:corsHeaders}) lines 131-135 (null body, no Content-Type).
ERROR: NOT symmetric with success. Error bodies use {error} and optionally {code}; they never include {success:false} and never {message}.
- 401 {error:'Unauthorized'} lines 139-147.
- 401 {error:'Authentication failed'} lines 176-184.
- Central catch lines 731-746: status = HttpError.status else 500 (line 734); body = {error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Unknown error'} (735-737); body.code added only when error instanceof HttpError (738). So: HttpError -> real 400/403/404/500 + {error,code}; any other Error -> 500 + {error}.

(2) SWALLOWED FAILURES (all FACT with line refs)
- L105: if(error) console.error('[AI SMS] default_organization_for_user failed:',error); -> no rethrow; falls through to L108 ORGANIZATION_REQUIRED. Error text lost.
- L113-116: isOrgAiReplyEnabled catch-equivalent: if(error){console.error(...); return true;} -> FAIL-OPEN: DB error silently enables AI replies.
- L897-938 analyzeImage: whole try/catch returns {description:'Image analysis failed',error} on failure (931-937), no rethrow; caller (L248) treats it as normal result.
- L926: analyzeImage reads response.json() WITHOUT checking response.ok -> an HTTP error body is parsed and yields 'Unable to analyze image' (L928), masking the real status/error.
- L1003-1005: catch(calErr){console.error(...)} calendar availability fetch -> swallowed, no rethrow.

## Artifact

**Findings**

RESPONSE SHAPE (FACT): Every response body is built by json() at L295-300 and ALWAYS carries a {proposals} key plus, on degraded/error paths, an {error} string. There is NO {message} key and NO {success} boolean anywhere in the file. OPTIONS returns a null body (L77).

SUCCESS shapes (FACT): (a) normal -> 200 {proposals: inserted ?? [], batch_id, through_seq} (L286); (b) dedupe cache hit -> 200 {proposals: existing, batch_id, through_seq, cached: true} (L205); (c) no-final-transcript -> 200 {proposals: [], error: 'No final transcript lines yet', through_seq} (L191) i.e. status 200 carrying an error key; (d) LLM failure -> 200 {proposals: [], error: message, through_seq} (L245) also 200-with-error, by design per header comment L12.

ERROR shapes (FACT): 405 {proposals:[], error:'POST only'} (L78); 500 {proposals:[], error:'Supabase configuration missing'} (L85); 401 {proposals:[], error:'Missing authorization'} (L93); 401 {proposals:[], error:'Unauthorized'} (L96); 429 {proposals:[], error:'Too many coach requests; slow down'} (L103); 400 {proposals:[], error:'call_log_id (uuid) is required'} (L111); 404 'Call log not found' (L121); 409 'Call log has no organization' (L122); 403 'Not a member of this organization' (L135); 403 'Lead is not in this organization' (L147); catch-all 500 {proposals:[], error: err.message|'Unknown error'} (L289). All error bodies use the key 'error' (never 'message'), and none include 'success'.

SWALLOWED FAILURES (FACT): (1) L109 `await req.json().catch(() => ({}))` swallows the body-parse rejection and coerces to {} (then 400 at L111) - an ignored promise rejection. (2) L197-203 dedupe SELECT ignores its error entirely: only `data` is destructured, no `error`; on query failure existing is null and the code silently proceeds to pay for a fresh LLM call. (3) L155-161 campaign/script SELECT also destructures only `data` (const { data: campaignRow }); error ignored, script silently null. (4) L219 console.warn on coach_recent_corrections RPC error, then no rethrow (corrections degrade to []); loop continues. (5) L284 console.warn on expireErr for the supersede UPDATE, no rethrow; still returns 200. (6) L242-246 LLM catch logs console.error then returns 200 (intentional/documented at L12, but converts a failure into success at the HTTP layer).

NO other swallow patterns (FACT): every other supabase await that destructures error either throws (L120, L134, L146, L171, L172, L185, L274). No `.catch(()=>{})` fire-and-forget and no un-awaited promises other than checkRateLimit at L100, which is invoked as if synchronous.

RATE-LIMIT catch (FACT): L99-106 converts only RateLimitError to 429 (L102-103); all other throws are re-thrown (L105).

CORS (FACT): corsHeaders is a module constant L21-24 = {Access-Control-Allow-Origin:'*', Access-Control-Allow-Headers:'authorization, x-client-info, apikey, content-type'}. No Access-Control-Allow-Methods and no Max-Age. OPTIONS preflight returns new Response(null,{headers:corsHeaders}) L77 (no Content-Type). All other responses go through json() which spreads corsHeaders + Content-Type:application/json + Cache-Control:no-store (L296-299). Wildcard '*' origin (L22).

ENV/SECRETS (FACT): L81-83 read SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, SUPABASE_ANON_KEY via Deno.env.get; if ANY is falsy a 500 {error:'Supabase configuration missing'} is returned (L84-85) - missing explicitly handled. The LLM key/secret is NOT read in this file; it is encapsulated in chatJSON from ../_shared/lithos.ts (imported L18, called L233).

THEORY: the 200-with-error convention (L191, L245) means a caller checking only res.ok cannot distinguish 'LLM down' / 'no transcript' from real success; failures read as success.

THEORY: the three error-ignoring reads (L155, L197, L209-221) are the main silent-degradation risk: dedupe failure doubles LLM spend, campaign failure drops the script from the prompt, corrections failure drops the learning block - all with no signal to the caller.

Analyzed twilio-sms-webhook/index.ts (1703 lines) for error handling. KEY: (1) SUCCESS = empty TwiML, status 200, Content-Type text/xml (no JSON keys). Only ONE non-200 path exists in the file: signature failure -> 403 text/plain 'Forbidden: invalid Twilio signature' (index.ts:490-496). No {error}/{message}/{success} JSON anywhere; top-level catch returns 200 (1694-1703). (2) Swallowed failures: empty catch (416-418); config-missing throw swallowed to 200 (461-463); DB-error logged then 200 (541-544); ~14 console.error-no-rethrow catches (679,1279,1327,1356,1360,1487,1495,1576,1583,1676,1683); non-ok HTTP logged only (674,1229,1353); many awaited Supabase calls ignore error (563,593,632,639,699,706,733,737,750,792,810,851,1308,1333,1462,1555,1664,1671); fired-await fetches with unchecked response (1469-1485,1563-1574); silent reschedule failure (1452-1458). ZERO .catch(()=>{}) present. (3) CORS = static corsHeaders (8-11), no Allow-Methods; env via Deno.env.get (TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN fail-closed 423-427, SUPABASE_* throw->swallowed 461-463, LOVABLE_API_KEY missing->skip 933-936).

## Artifact

**Findings**

HTTP SUCCESS SHAPE: the handler returns TwiML, never JSON. Every success path returns new Response('<empty TwiML>', { headers: {...corsHeaders, Content-Type text/xml} }) with implicit status 200 (helper twimlResponse at index.ts:352 defaults status=200). Success body has NO JSON keys (no success/message). ERROR SHAPE: the ONLY non-200 path in the whole file is signature failure: status 403, plain-text body 'Forbidden: invalid Twilio signature', Content-Type text/plain (index.ts:490-496). No {error}, {message} or {success} JSON is ever emitted. The top-level catch returns status 200 (index.ts:1694-1703), so internal failures are indistinguishable from success by status code. SWALLOWED FAILURES (each cited): empty catch with only a comment (index.ts:416-418); top-level catch returns 200 instead of 5xx (index.ts:1694-1703); missing SUPABASE_URL/SERVICE_ROLE_KEY throws then is caught to 200 (index.ts:461-463); DB-error branch logs then returns 200 TwiML (index.ts:541-544); console.error-with-no-rethrow catches for disposition routing (679-681), check (1279-1281), booking (1360-1362), reschedule (1495-1497), cancel (1583-1585), three syncError blocks (1356-1358, 1487-1489, 1576-1578), sendError (1676-1678), aiError (1683-1685), apptError (1327-1329); non-ok HTTP responses logged only without throwing (disposition 674-678, AI gateway 1229-1231, calendar sync 1353-1354); failed conversation create logged then continues (588-589); message-store failure logged then full AI processing continues (623-627); isOrgAiReplyEnabled swallows the DB error and returns true (443-446); many awaited Supabase calls destructure only data and ignore error (563, 593, 632, 639-642, 699, 706, 733, 737, 750, 792, 810, 851, 1308, 1333, 1462, 1555, 1664, 1671); fire-and-forget awaited fetches whose HTTP response is never checked (calendar update_event 1469-1485, delete_event 1563-1574); silent no-log failure where reschedule only acts if !updateError and has no else (1452-1458). NOTE: grep found ZERO .catch( occurrences - there is no .catch(()=>{}) anywhere; the defect is ignored return/error values, not unhandled promise rejections. Grep for any Instantly/Mailgun write endpoint returns ZERO matches. - status: completed
- tldr: Dial Smart: none of the 5 claimed differentiators is a real moat; all are copyable. Defensibility is off-list (data gravity, 199 migrations/495 RLS policies, carrier/GHL depth).

MOAT ANALYSIS complete. Verdict per claimed differentiator (moat vs copyable), all code-cited: (1) Multi-vendor telephony - COPYABLE: the three provider adapters (retell/telnyx/twilio) and CarrierRouter are TODO stubs (twilioAdapter.ts:7, carrierRouter.ts:12,78-81), but multi-vendor is real at the edge-function dispatch layer (outbound-calling/index.ts:162,308-318,885-938). (2) White-label metered credits - COPYABLE mechanism, real data-gravity asset once populated: real schema (20260124_white_label_credits.sql:27-86), wired end-to-end (stripe-webhook:382,417; retell-call-webhook:2114; api-gateway:1043). (3) AI managers - COPYABLE and currently non-functional in prod: ai-autonomous-engine is 5645 LOC and real (index.ts:401,752) but its cron is unscheduled/launch-quarantined (20260713061000:5,16-26). (4) Pack system - COPYABLE thin abstraction: packs.ts is 122 LOC, all PackDefinition.routes empty (packs.ts:54,67,80); backend gating is real but the architecture is a registry, not a plugin framework. (5) Door to Door vertical - WEAK-to-MODERATE moat, deepest of the five, but a verbatim PORT of DoorBoss (DoorToDoorApp.tsx:4). REAL defensibility is off-list: data gravity + 199 migrations/495 RLS policies + carrier/GHL integration depth + D2D content.

## Artifact

**Findings**

VERDICT SUMMARY: Of the five claimed differentiators, NONE is a defensible moat in the hard-to-copy sense; all five are copyable features (weeks to months for a competent team). The durable switching-cost asset is cumulative and OFF-list: multi-tenant data gravity plus 199 migrations/495 RLS policies plus carrier/GHL integration depth plus the D2D vertical content. The codebase is genuinely valuable (a real product), but its differentiators are features, not moats.

ITEM 1 - Multi-vendor telephony: COPYABLE (real at the dispatch layer; the unified adapter + intelligent routing abstraction is unfinished scaffolding). FACT: all three provider adapters are TODO stubs that always return failure (twilioAdapter.ts:7,52-65; telnyxAdapter.ts:7,57-70; retellAdapter.ts:7,49-60) and CarrierRouter is a stub (carrierRouter.ts:12 TODO PR E, :78-81 empty loadProviderConfigs). BUT multi-vendor is REAL at the edge-function dispatch layer: outbound-calling/index.ts:162 supports provider retell|telnyx, :308-318 uses real API keys, :885-938 verifies live agents; twilio-sms-webhook is 1706 LOC of real SMS. The working capability is thin routing (local-presence area-code match, STIR/SHAKEN preference) anyone can replicate in weeks.

ITEM 2 - White-label metered credits: COPYABLE mechanism; the ledger becomes a real data-gravity asset only once populated. FACT: real schema - 20260124_white_label_credits.sql (org credits table :27-58, transactions ledger :92+, RLS :70-86) plus v2_enhanced (28KB), credit_ledger_schema_contract (40KB), agent_pricing_schema_contract (14KB). Wired end to end: add/reserve/finalize RPCs, credit-management (32KB), stripe-webhook:382,417 checkout-to-add_credits idempotent, retell-call-webhook:2114 post-call deduction, api-gateway:1043 daily-cap gate. Metered billing is standard SaaS - copyable in weeks.

ITEM 3 - AI managers: COPYABLE feature AND currently non-functional in production. FACT: ai-autonomous-engine is 5645 LOC and does real work (queues ai_action_queue :401, executes outbound-calling :752, 24 output dimensions), and MissionBriefingWizard.tsx/AutonomousAgentDashboard.tsx exist. BUT its cron is disabled: migration 20260713061000:5 says it is launch-quarantined and :16-26 unschedules ai-autonomous-engine-job with no enable switch. An LLM optimize-loop is replicable in weeks.

ITEM 4 - Pack system: COPYABLE thin abstraction; value is in pack content, not the registry. FACT: packs.ts is 122 LOC; backend gating is real (20261029010000_industry_packs.sql: org_has_pack SECURITY DEFINER :9-31, set_org_packs admin-only :42-84, allow-list :49). BUT all PackDefinition.routes are empty (packs.ts:54,67,80) so route gating is unimplemented; enablement is a jsonb array plus one sidebar tab and a single Dashboard case d2d-app.

ITEM 5 - Door to Door vertical: WEAK-to-MODERATE moat (deepest of the five) but it is a PORT of DoorBoss, so the IP/content originate elsewhere. FACT: 12 files, 7666 LOC; host.ts (~2078 lines) maps 20+ DoorBoss routes onto 9 d2d_* tables over 3 migrations; enroll.ts bridges doorstep follow-ups with consent/DNC gating (:167-173); coachRules.ts (28.6KB) and doorboss.css (35KB) are verbatim DoorBoss ports; DoorToDoorApp.tsx:4 says 'a port, not a re-implementation'; 4 tests incl. DoorToDoorGhlOptional. A competitor who built a canvassing app once can rebuild this in months.

OFF-LIST SWITCHING-COST ASSETS (the real defensibility): (a) 199 migrations and 495 CREATE POLICY statements = long multi-tenant schema/RLS history, expensive to replicate and risky to migrate away from; (b) data gravity - leads, campaigns, call_logs, sms, scheduled_follow_ups and the credit ledger all in one Postgres (ref emonjusymdripmkvtttc); (c) GHL integration depth - ghl-integration (1225), ghl-webhook-trigger (424), ghl-batch-callback (617), ghl-shadow-ingest (148), GHLFieldMappingTab (1352), useGoHighLevel (867); (d) operational maturity - unattended safety-backstop migrations. These, not the five claimed differentiators, are what a competitor cannot clone quickly.

# market-pricing-schema

- status: completed
- tldr: Unit = the cent ('credit'); 1 credit = $0.01 (implicit, /100). Retail voice $0.15/min, provider $0.07/min, no retail SMS price; SKUs $25-$1000.

PRICING SCHEMA -> NATURAL PRICE POINT (node market-pricing-schema) = DONE.

ANSWER: Unit metered = the CENT (internally a 'credit'), no separate token. Credit->dollar = 1 credit = 1 cent = $0.01, 1:1 and IMPLICIT (schema stores no dollar/credit-rate column; the 1:1 comes from the server purchase catalog and every /100 display).
- Retail voice = $0.15/min default (org_credits.cost_per_minute_cents DEFAULT 15), per-agent override via agent_pricing.customer_price_per_min_cents.
- Provider voice = $0.07/min default (retell_cost_per_minute_cents DEFAULT 7); composed base 13.5 c/min (LLM5+voice7+telephony1.5).
- SMS: NO retail price in the billing schema; only an internal ~1 cent/message estimate plus provider pass-through. reserve/finalize are minutes-only.
- Retail SKUs (the real dollar price points): $25/$50/$100/$250/$500/$1000 with bonus credits (5000,250)(10000,750)(25000,2500)(50000,7500)(100000,20000).
- NATURAL price point: voice $0.15/min, SMS ~$0.01, min SKU $25; default gross margin $0.08/min = 53%; mixed call+SMS ~= $0.385 (THEORY, no duration seed).

EVIDENCE (file:line): 20260124_white_label_credits.sql:31,35-36; 20260713070000_agent_pricing_schema_contract.sql:7-32; 20260713060000_credit_ledger_schema_contract.sql; credit-management/index.ts:194,200-206,590-624; _shared/credit-purchase-policy.ts:13-21,238-251; stripe-webhook/index.ts:365-398; budget-tracker/index.ts:241; ai-autonomous-engine/index.ts:1077,1806; ClientPortal.tsx:107-114; CreditDashboard.tsx:366; live baseline calculate_agent_base_cost:190-219.

**Findings**

1) METERED UNIT = the cent (internally a 'credit'). Balances/prices/deductions are all cents; columns balance_cents, *_per_min_cents. 2) CREDIT->DOLLAR = 1 credit = 1 cent = $0.01, 1:1, IMPLICIT (derived via /100); schema has NO stored dollar/credit-per-dollar column. 3) RETAIL VOICE PRICE = DEFAULT 15 c/min = $0.15/min. 4) PROVIDER VOICE COST = DEFAULT 7 c/min = $0.07/min. 5) COMPOSED PROVIDER BASE COST default 13.5 c/min = LLM 5 + voice 7 + telephony 1.5 + KB 0. 6) PRICING ROWS: pricing_tiers (platform-global provider-cost catalog: tier_type, tier_name, base_cost_per_min_cents) and agent_pricing (per-tenant dispatch-time customer price: customer_price_per_min_cents, markup_cents/percentage, base_cost_per_min_cents); both read-only to authenticated, service_role writes; margin cannot be negative and active rows need a price. 7) NO RETAIL SMS PRICE: SMS is only an internal ~1c/message ESTIMATE plus provider passthrough; reserve/finalize are minutes-only. 8) RETAIL CATALOG = 6 SKUs $25/$50/$100/$250/$500/$1000 with server-controlled bonus credits (2500,0)(5000,250)(10000,750)(25000,2500)(50000,7500)(100000,20000). 9) BILLING is opt-in (organizations.billing_enabled default false) and short-circuits all charges. 10) TWO-PHASE reserve->finalize: reserve holds max_exposure and snapshots customer_rate/provider_rate/pricing_policy_version='credit-reservation-v1' immutably; finalize charges ceil(actual_minutes*customer_rate), margin = deduction - provider_cost, and refuses mutable rates.
